props.title: The Last Days of Planet Earth
props.initialSlug: Japanese disaster epic unleashes 10 biblical plagues

sections.content: **The Last Days of Planet Earth (1974)** (1974), also known as "Prophecies of Nostradamus," represents Toho Studios' ambitious dive into apocalyptic sci-fi horror during Japan's environmental crisis era. Director Toshio Masuda crafted this controversial disaster epic drawing parallels with **Godzilla** (1954) in its environmental messaging, though with a darker, more pessimistic outlook. The film's structure, following multiple catastrophic predictions, influenced later anthology-style disaster films like **Earthquake** (1974) and **2012** (2009). sections.content: The 1970s marked a golden age for apocalyptic cinema, with environmental concerns driving narratives. Silent Running (1972) took the eco-disaster concept to space, while **Soylent Green** (1973) presented a horrifying future of overpopulation and food scarcity. These films reflected growing awareness of pollution and environmental degradation, themes that **The Last Days of Planet Earth** (1974) amplified through its blend of prophecy and scientific speculation.

Japanese disaster films of this era often incorporated elements of kaiju and science fiction, seen in works like **Submersion of Japan** (1973) and **Prophecy of Death** (1974). What sets **The Last Days of Planet Earth** apart is its anthology-like structure and unflinching portrayal of mutations and environmental collapse, elements that would later influence films like **Children of Men** (2006) and **Snowpiercer** (2013). sections.content: The film's controversial nature - it was heavily edited for international release due to disturbing imagery - speaks to Japanese cinema's unique approach to disaster narratives. While American films like **The China Syndrome** (1979) focused on single catastrophic events, Japanese productions like **The Last Days of Planet Earth** presented cascading disasters, reflecting post-war anxieties about technological advancement and environmental destruction.
